title: tuwunel chart values
description: Validated against the tuwunel chart templates. Keys where the chart accepts several representations (CPU/memory quantities, service ports) intentionally accept both forms; keys the templates interpolate verbatim are restricted to what renders into a valid manifest.

quantity.description: Kubernetes resource quantity: a number or a string with an optional suffix (m, Mi, Gi, ...).

stringMap.description: String-to-string map, as required by Kubernetes labels and annotations.

scalarMap.description: String-to-scalar map; keys become container env names, so they have to be names Kubernetes accepts ([-._a-zA-Z][-._a-zA-Z0-9]*), and values are quoted into environment variables.

secretEnvMap.description: Environment variables sourced from Secrets. Keys become container env names, so they have to be names Kubernetes accepts ([-._a-zA-Z][-._a-zA-Z0-9]*). Values must be '<secret-name>/<key>'; the chart splits on '/' and fails at render time otherwise.

envVarList.description: Raw Kubernetes env entries passed through with toYaml. The name has to be one Kubernetes accepts; the rest of the entry (value, valueFrom, ...) is passed through as written.

tag.description: Rendered verbatim after the ':' separator, so it cannot be empty (an empty tag renders 'name:', which the kubelet refuses as InvalidImageName); the main tuwunel image tag additionally goes through tpl().

rtcIngressSpec.description: RTC ingress. The RTC host serves a fixed path set (the JWT service's endpoints, everything else to LiveKit), so unlike the main ingress there is no path or extraHosts knob.

routeParentRef.description: A Gateway API parentRef. The field set belongs to Gateway API, not to this chart, so unknown members are allowed here - the rendered route is validated against the real CRD schema in CI.

gatewaySpec.description: Gateway API exposure for the homeserver. The chart renders HTTPRoutes that attach to a Gateway you run; it never creates the Gateway itself.

routeGatewaySpec.description: Gateway API exposure for the RTC host: the same Gateway(s) as the homeserver unless parentRefs is set. The path set is fixed (the JWT service's endpoints, everything else to LiveKit), so there is no hostnames knob.

mediaRouteSpec.description: Gateway API routes for the LiveKit media ports. Only meaningful with rtc.livekit.networkMode: pod, where the Service fronts those ports (a template fails the render otherwise); whether UDP/TCP proxying works is a property of the Gateway implementation, not of this chart.

rtcSidecarSpec.description: Shape shared by the RTC JWT service and the LiveKit server.

probeSpec.description: One exec probe against `tuwunel --health-check`. The timeout is per attempt, so the worst case is periodSeconds x failureThreshold.

backupSpec.description: tuwunel's built-in online database backups: a volume mounted at backup.path and the configuration keys that point the server at it.

path.description: Absolute mount path inside the container; rendered as database_backup_path.

keep.description: Rendered as database_backups_to_keep; older backups are pruned after a new one.

schedule.description: Five-field cron expression for the sidecar that signals the server with SIGUSR2.

command.description: Rendered as admin_signal_execute: the admin console command a SIGUSR2 runs.

server_name.description: Matrix server name (the domain part of every user ID).

includeServerName.description: Whether the server_name host is rendered into the host fields: the Ingress rule and its TLS host, and the HTTPRoute hostname. A boolean; `false` is for a deployment whose apex is served elsewhere, and the exposure templates refuse the render when it leaves an Ingress or an HTTPRoute without any host.

serverNameWellKnownOnly.description: Whether the server_name host serves the discovery documents alone: its Ingress rule loses the /_matrix path, and the route the chart renders for that host loses it as well, keeping /.well-known/matrix as its single prefix. A boolean; `true` is for a deployment whose apex resolves to the cluster but should answer nothing beyond delegation, and it needs config.global.well_known.server - the exposure templates refuse the render when server_name would be the only host they serve, since narrowing that one leaves every other path unroutable.

image.description: Main tuwunel image. Its tag is rendered through tpl(), so it may reference other values.

busybox.description: Image for the scheduled-backup sidecar and the `helm test` pod. Has to be multi-arch.

config.description: Rendered verbatim into config.toml, so any tuwunel/Conduit configuration key is accepted here. The keys pinned under global are the ones whose type stops the server from starting when it is wrong (quoted booleans, an unparsable bind address, a misspelled ip_source), or that the chart also derives from a value of its own.

address.description: Address or list of addresses tuwunel listens on; "::" is a dual-stack socket, "0.0.0.0" is IPv4 only.

allow_federation.description: Must be a boolean: the string "false" makes tuwunel exit at startup.

allow_registration.description: Must be a boolean: the string "true" makes tuwunel exit at startup.

log.description: Log level: trace, debug, info, warn, error.

ip_source.description: Where the client IP comes from behind a proxy. A misspelled value makes every request fail with 500 M_UNKNOWN on a header-based source (or silently mis-attribute every IP), so the accepted set is pinned to upstream's.

db_pool_max_workers.description: RocksDB background worker/pool size; upstream's 2048 default can exceed the pod's task limit on a many-core node and fail startup with EAGAIN.

database_backup_path.description: Where online backups are written; the chart renders this from backup.path when backup.enabled.

database_backups_to_keep.description: How many backups are kept; the chart renders this from backup.keep when backup.enabled.

server_name.description: Accepted for compatibility, but it must match the server_name value: the chart sets TUWUNEL_SERVER_NAME, which wins over the file.

port.description: Accepted for compatibility, but it must match service.port: the chart sets TUWUNEL_PORT, which wins over the file.

extraEnv.description: Additional environment variables for the tuwunel container; both name and value are required, and the name has to be one Kubernetes accepts.

args.description: Extra arguments for the tuwunel container, e.g. --restore-backup.

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description: Has to cover the one-time database migration on the first start after an upgrade (upstream asks for 30 minutes); a SIGKILL in the middle of it leaves the database half-migrated.

type.description: ClusterIP, NodePort or LoadBalancer. ExternalName is not offered: the chart has no externalName value, so the API server would refuse the Service it renders.

clusterIP.description: 'None' makes the Service headless (the stable per-pod DNS the StatefulSet needs) and is only accepted on a ClusterIP Service; an address pins the VIP. On LoadBalancer/NodePort, 'None' or an empty string means the cluster allocates one - the field is then omitted.

port.description: The chart's single port: rendered into the Service, the Ingress backends, the container port and TUWUNEL_PORT. Both 8080 and "8080" are accepted.

storageClass.description: Chart-wide rule: unset or "" leaves storageClassName out (the default provisioner decides), "-" renders storageClassName: "" (bind a pre-created PV), anything else is quoted.

size.description: PVC storage request, quoted into the manifest; a unit suffix is expected.

then.description: With RTC enabled, the domain is what the discovery record, the JWT service and the ingress are built from - a missing one would render an unroutable deployment. It is written verbatim into an Ingress/HTTPRoute host and into a URL ('https://<domain>'), so only a bare lowercase DNS name works.

domain.description: Bare lowercase DNS name, checked when RTC is enabled; the unused default is an empty string, which is why the rule lives on the enabled branch.

livekit.description: LiveKit media server. Shares the sidecar shape with rtc.jwt plus LiveKit-specific settings.

networkMode.description: hostNetwork shares the node's network namespace (fixed ports, a UDP range is fine); pod routes media through rtc.livekit.service, which can only forward the single config.rtc.udp_port.

config.description: Rendered verbatim into livekit.yaml; any LiveKit configuration key is accepted here. The chart adds keys (keys, room.auto_create, webhook.*) that the JWT pairing needs, only when they are absent.
